skill.name: etetoolkit
skill.description: Use ETE Toolkit for phylogenetic tree analysis, taxonomy integration, evolutionary event detection, and tree visualization workflows.
skill.summary: Analyze, annotate, compare, and visualize phylogenetic trees with ETE Toolkit guidance.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, biological taxonomy examples, and normal local output handling. The confirmed issues are disclosed but security-relevant: ETE may write a large taxonomy cache under a hidden home directory, and the documentation includes sudo package installation commands. No prompt injection, credential theft, malicious networking, or data exfiltration intent was found in the reviewed evidence.

remediation.issue: Privileged package installation commands are included in user-facing documentation.
remediation.suggestion: Replace sudo installation steps with a warning that system dependencies require user approval, and never instruct the assistant to run privileged commands automatically.

remediation.issue: NCBITaxa may download a large database into ~/.etetoolkit/taxa.sqlite on first use.
remediation.suggestion: Document the download size, destination path, and consent requirement before running NCBITaxa examples.

content.value_statement: Phylogenetic analysis often requires tree parsing, taxonomy lookup, evolutionary event detection, and figure generation. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through practical ETE Toolkit workflows for research data.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to load, write, prune, reroot, and compare trees in Newick and related formats.
Guides PhyloTree workflows for duplication, speciation, orthology, and paralogy analysis.
Shows NCBITaxa workflows for taxid translation, lineage lookup, and taxonomy-based tree annotation.
Provides examples for rendering tree figures as PDF, SVG, PNG, and interactive ETE views.
Includes command-line helper usage for tree statistics, conversion, pruning, rerooting, and ASCII output.
Documents batch processing patterns for multiple tree files and large tree traversal.
limitations: Requires the ETE Python package and optional GUI dependencies for rendering features.
NCBI taxonomy examples may download a large local database on first use.
The skill provides guidance and examples; it does not validate biological conclusions automatically.
Large trees can require careful memory handling and may need iterator-based processing.

use_cases.title: Prepare gene trees for analysis
use_cases.description: Convert, reroot, prune, and summarize phylogenetic trees before downstream research workflows.

use_cases.title: Annotate trees with taxonomy
use_cases.description: Map species names to taxids, retrieve lineages, and add taxonomy metadata to tree leaves.

use_cases.title: Create publication figures
use_cases.description: Design styled tree visualizations and export them as vector or raster graphics for papers.

prompt_templates.title: Load and summarize a tree
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ETE Toolkit skill to show me how to load my Newick tree, count leaves, list node names, and save a cleaned copy.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare trees for comparison
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through rerooting, pruning, resolving polytomies, and comparing two phylogenetic trees with ETE.

prompt_templates.title: Annotate with NCBI taxonomy
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me use ETE NCBITaxa to translate species names to taxids, retrieve lineages, and add taxonomy features to tree leaves.

prompt_templates.title: Build a full phylogenomics pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an ETE workflow that loads a gene tree with an alignment, detects duplication and speciation events, extracts ortholog groups, annotates taxonomy, and renders a final figure.

output_examples.input: Summarize my tree and prepare it for downstream analysis.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step ETE workflow that loads the tree, reports leaf and node counts, roots it at the midpoint, prunes selected taxa, and writes a new tree file.

output_examples.input: Create a taxonomy-annotated species tree for selected organisms.
output_examples.output: A guided workflow that translates organism names to taxids, builds the connecting taxonomy tree, adds scientific names and ranks, and saves the annotated result.

output_examples.input: Make a publication-ready figure from a tree.
output_examples.output: A visualization plan that selects layout settings, styles clades and support values, and exports PDF or SVG output for editing.

best_practices: Confirm input tree format and branch length meaning before modifying topology.
Ask before running workflows that download taxonomy data or install system dependencies.
Use iterator-based traversal for large trees to reduce memory usage.
anti_patterns: Do not run sudo installation commands without explicit user approval.
Do not treat species name parsing rules as universal across datasets.
Do not overwrite original tree files before saving reviewed processed copies.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps use ETE Toolkit for phylogenetic tree manipulation, evolutionary analysis, taxonomy integration, and visualization.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it install ETE automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents installation commands, but package installation should only happen after user approval.

faq.question: Does NCBI taxonomy use local storage?
faq.answer: Yes. ETE NCBITaxa can download a large taxonomy database to a hidden home directory on first use.

faq.question: Can it create visual tree figures?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for ETE rendering to PDF, SVG, PNG, and interactive views when dependencies are available.

faq.question: Is it limited to biological phylogenies?
faq.answer: It focuses on biological phylogenetics but also documents hierarchical clustering tree workflows.
